newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil down on low India award.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil down on low India award.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were down at midday on Monday after India's decision to buy an unexpectedly low amount of diesel for August delivery and at the same time cancelling its term tenders, traders said.
"The market is down this morning because of India," a trader said.
July swaps were indicated at $21.65/$21.85 per barrel while August was better defined at $22.20/$22.30, both down 30 cents from Friday, brokers said.

Traders said the market moved down after news of Indian OIl Corp's decision to buy a mere 165,000 tonnes of diesel for August delivery compared to the bumper 855,000 tonnes it bought for July arrival.
The award is also well below market expectations of about 400,000 tonnes as late as Friday evening, they said.
India also sent more bearish news by cancelling its term tender to buy diesel and kerosene for August 1997-March 1998 delivery.
Traders said India cancelled the tender because none of the diesel offers met its expectations of a discount to spot Middle East quotes.
Shell Singapore's expected lower crude run average for July of 49,000 tonne per day (TPD) compared to its 59,000 TPD capacity is likely to ease the prompt glut slightly, traders said.

But others said more production cuts or a new round of buying are needed to clear out all the prompt physical overhang. The jet fuel/gas oil spread is steady with July regrade last quoted at $1.80/$2.00 per barrel.
Fuel oil was also unchanged in a flat market with July, August and September swaps quoted at $98.50/$99.50 per tonne, brokers said.
